solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: PIN providing on-line security?

parts.note: on-line here means on the washing line, not on the internet; the pin is the wooden one that holds laundry there

explanation.surface: Talk of a PIN number keeping your internet banking safe.
explanation.walkthrough: PIN in capitals and 'on-line' push you towards passwords and cyber security; read it literally as a pin that keeps washing secure on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden or plastic clip used to fasten laundry to a washing line is that sort of pin.

clue.text: Collision of new cars preceding hospital

indicators.note: preceding places the rearranged cars before the hospital letter
new indicates the letters take a fresh arrangement

parts.note: H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A smash between new cars, followed by a trip to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like it describes the cars in the surface, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash is a violent impact, as when vehicles hit each other.

clue.text: Rebecca lost a silly sports day contest?

indicators.note: silly suggests muddled nonsense, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Rebecca loses a daft race at her school sports day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges REBECCA LOST A. The question mark admits a sports day is an example, not a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle race is a running event over hurdles, nets and the like, a staple of school athletics days.

clue.text: Some rubbish in this clue

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A solver complaining that this clue is partly rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint is a clue or suggestion that helps someone work something out.

clue.text: Toast is lightly brown across length

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the browning word spans the length letter

parts.note: to sauté is to fry quickly, lightly browning the food

explanation.surface: Instructions for toast: brown it lightly all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' looks culinary, matching the surface, but it means a gesture of honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To salute someone is to honour them, as raising a glass in a toast does.

clue.text: Put-up job pinching diamonds: trouble for place of riches

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing hold of, so the diamonds letter is held inside
in a down clue, put up means written upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a role is a job or position
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A rigged jewel heist ends in trouble for a wealthy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put-up job' looks like a set phrase for a rigged crime; split it so 'Put-up' reverses the job word and 'pinching' wraps it round D.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary city of gold sought by Spanish explorers, now any land of fabulous wealth.

clue.text: Arrive early to avoid disappointment for guests?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: travel quickly and get somewhere sooner than planned
second meaning, read literally: make sure the guests enjoy themselves

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is normally about fast travel; the question mark flags the literal reading of making a good time for people at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make fast progress on a journey; taken word by word it means to create an enjoyable occasion.

clue.text: Cold bottle of milk, on reflection, is what kitty loves?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the bottle's word is reversed

parts.note: a pinta is British slang for a pint of milk, from the old advertising slogan

explanation.surface: A cold bottle of milk, as a cat might be thought to adore.
explanation.walkthrough: A pinta is informal British for a pint of milk; 'on reflection' turns it into ATNIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Catnip is a mint-family plant whose scent excites domestic cats, hence a cat's favourite.

clue.text: Arena's redeveloped by large football club

indicators.note: an arena that is redeveloped is rebuilt, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A stadium being rebuilt by a big football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redeveloped' rearranges ARENAS into ARSENA; add L for large.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a well-known London Premier League football club.

clue.text: A student following doctor in emotive situation

indicators.note: following places A and the student after the doctor in the answer

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a student on a postgraduate course

explanation.surface: A student trailing behind a doctor at a tense, emotional moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama, in the everyday sense, is an exciting or emotionally charged event or state of affairs.

clue.text: Initially head off a sign of voting fraud

indicators.note: Initially asks for the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: a voter marks the ballot paper with a cross, X

explanation.surface: Someone trying to head off the first signs of electoral fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes the first letters of 'head' and 'off', giving HO; then A and X.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax is a deception or trick meant to fool people, a kind of fraud.

clue.text: Swimmer's temperature taken internally by medic

indicators.note: something taken internally goes inside, so the temperature letter sits within the medic

parts.note: a surgeon is a medical doctor who operates

explanation.surface: A swimmer having their temperature taken by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Swimmer is 'is': the swimmer is the answer, and the rest of the clue builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish, and fish are 'swimmers' in crossword shorthand.

clue.text: A rep twice arranged to come back

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: A REP is taken twice over, as the clue's next word says, giving eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sales rep scheduled to return for a second visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' means A REP is written out two times, AREPAREP, before 'arranged' shuffles it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappear is to come into view again, to return after an absence.

clue.text: Girl swimming Loch Fyne's far end

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters move about freely, so they are rearranged
far end picks the last letter of the loch's name

parts.note: Loch Fyne is a sea loch in Scotland; the possessive points to its name

explanation.surface: A girl swimming to the far end of Loch Fyne, a long Scottish sea loch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges LOCH to CHLO; the far end of Fyne is E.
explanation.definitionFit: Chloe is a female first name, and a girl's name is a common crossword target.

clue.text: One apprehending eclipse over rocky hill

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo or eclipse it
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor in south-west England

explanation.surface: Someone watching an eclipse from a rocky hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky outcrop on a hill, common in Devon and Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A captor is a person who catches or seizes someone, so one who apprehends them.

clue.text: Bad day switching round sink

indicators.note: switching round means the pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: poor means bad, of low quality

explanation.surface: A miserable day spent going round in circles at the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching round' turns POOR D backwards. 'sink' is a verb here, not the kitchen fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or hang down limply, as to sink lower.

clue.text: Short test covering four inconsequential facts

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the shortened test goes round the four
Short means cut off, so the test word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trial is a test
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A quick quiz on four bits of trivial knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts TRIAL to TRIA, which goes 'covering' IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivia are small, unimportant details or pieces of knowledge, as in a pub quiz.

clue.text: Sweat resulting from piper's bungled note

indicators.note: bungled means messed up, so the letters are put in a jumbled order

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A bagpiper sweating after fluffing a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bungled' looks like it describes the piper's playing, but it is the anagram signal; 'resulting from' only links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To perspire is to sweat, the formal or polite word for it.

clue.text: Cheese kept in Notre Dame

indicators.note: kept in says the answer is held within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Notre and the start of Dame

explanation.surface: Cheese being stored inside the Paris cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese, typically sold in a ball with a red wax coat.

clue.text: The setter and martial arts star brawl

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so ME
Bruce Lee was the famous martial arts film star

explanation.surface: The crossword setter getting into a fight with Bruce Lee.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused, disorderly scuffle involving several people, a free-for-all.

clue.text: Shock as attacked by insect? Not good!

indicators.note: Not good says the good letter is to be left out

parts.note: stung means attacked by a bee or wasp

explanation.surface: Being stung by a wasp is a nasty shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish or daze someone, so to shock them.

clue.text: Previously stuffed by United exactly when expected

indicators.note: stuffed by means filled with, so United's letter goes inside

parts.note: once means previously, at some earlier time
U is the abbreviation for United in football team names

explanation.surface: A team previously thrashed by United, exactly as everyone predicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffed' looks like slang for a heavy defeat, but it signals filling ONCE with U.
explanation.definitionFit: On cue means at precisely the right moment, like an actor responding to a prompt.

clue.text: Angry words from group of three dividing six pounds

indicators.note: dividing means splitting something apart, so the trio sits between the six and the pounds

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pounds
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: Three people falling out over six pounds and exchanging angry words.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriol is bitter, caustic criticism or abuse, named after the corrosive acid.

clue.text: Younger relative and I tan remarkably in Mediterranean country

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the name of the country

parts.note: Greece lies on the Mediterranean Sea

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something unusual has happened, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young relative and I get remarkably tanned on holiday in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkably' rearranges I TAN to ATNI, which goes 'in' GREECE.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-niece is the daughter of one's nephew or niece, a relative of a later generation.
